questions.question_text: What should be done first when constructing an angle with a protractor?

options.text: Draw a base arm and mark its endpoint as the vertex.
Draw two arms and then choose a degree mark.
options.why: The target angle must determine where the second arm goes.

options.text: Mark the degree before choosing a vertex.
options.why: The degree mark is positioned relative to the vertex and base arm.

options.text: Place the protractor centre at the end of the finished second arm.
options.why: The centre belongs at the common vertex of both arms.

questions.solution_text: Begin with a base arm and its endpoint vertex so the protractor can be aligned.

questions.question_text: After marking $75^{\circ}$ on the protractor, what is the next action?

options.text: Rule a second arm from the vertex through the mark.
Draw a line between the two protractor zero marks.
options.why: The second arm must pass through the chosen degree mark.

options.text: Move the vertex to the degree mark.
options.why: The vertex remains fixed at the endpoint of the base arm.

options.text: Measure 75 units along the base arm.
options.why: Degrees measure turn, not distance along the arm.

questions.solution_text: Use a ruler to join the vertex to the $75^{\circ}$ mark.

questions.question_text: A target is $115^{\circ}$, and the chosen mark carries paired readings $65$ and $115$. Which reading should be followed?

options.text: $115$ on the scale that begins at the base arm's zero
$65$ because it is the smaller printed number
options.why: Choosing the smaller number creates the supplementary acute angle.

options.text: both readings because they label the same target angle
options.why: The two scales measure from opposite ends and give different angles.

options.text: $180$ because paired readings should be added
options.why: Adding the paired readings gives a straight angle, not the target.

questions.solution_text: Follow the scale that begins at $0^{\circ}$ on the base arm and reaches $115^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: To construct a reflex angle of $235^{\circ}$, which smaller angle can be constructed first?

options.why: Only the amount beyond the 180-degree straight angle was constructed.
The 55-degree excess beyond a straight angle was subtracted from 360.
A semicircular protractor cannot directly mark beyond 180 degrees.

questions.question_text: Which error would make a carefully marked $80^{\circ}$ construction inaccurate?

options.text: Drawing the second arm from beside the vertex
Writing the degree symbol beside the finished angle
options.why: Correct notation does not alter the angle's construction.

options.text: Using a ruler to draw a straight second arm
options.why: A ruler is the correct tool for forming the arm through the mark.

options.text: Checking that the chosen scale starts at zero
options.why: This check prevents, rather than causes, a scale-reading error.

questions.solution_text: Both arms must share the same vertex; starting the second arm elsewhere changes the angle.
